name: Dodla Dairy Ltd
tagline: Well-run, near-debt-free South-India + East-Africa dairy with a strong FY25 (PAT +56%) -- but FY26 saw EBITDA margin compress to ~7.5% (two quarters at ~5%), value-added-product mix slip back to ~27%, and an inability to pass procurement-cost swings through; a quality operator in a structurally thin-margin, volume-capped business
business_overview: Dodla Dairy procures milk (~97% direct from farmers) across 5 South Indian states, sells liquid milk + value-added products (curd, ghee, butter, paneer, SMP) in ~13 states, runs a cattle-feed business (Orgafeed) and a higher-margin Africa operation (Uganda, Kenya). Recently acquired Osam Dairy (East India). ~14 processing plants in India (~20 LLPD capacity), 2 in Africa. Building a greenfield Maharashtra plant (~Rs 590 Cr, ~Rs 350 Cr spent).
fundamentals_table: Revenue Rs 3,720 Cr (+19%); EBITDA Rs 380 Cr (10.2% margin, +31%); PAT Rs 259-260 Cr (+56%)
Revenue Rs 4,125 Cr (+~11%); EBITDA Rs 308 Cr (7.5% margin, DOWN 19%); PAT Rs 267 Cr (flat, aided by a one-time tax credit)
EBITDA margin ~5% for two straight quarters; gross margin 23-25.6% vs ~27%+
Near debt-free; ~Rs 596 Cr cash on books
~27% of sales in FY26, down from ~35% peak
fundamentals_narrative: The multi-year record is decent -- ~19% FY25 revenue growth, expanding Africa and Orgafeed, disciplined procurement (won't squeeze farmers), strong balance sheet. But FY26 is a clear step down: EBITDA margin fell from ~10% to ~7.5%, two recent quarters printed ~5% margin, gross margin compressed on higher procurement costs the company could not pass on, and the VAP mix -- the whole margin-expansion thesis -- slipped back to ~27% (partly optical, from lower bulk butter/SMP sales, but still). Employee and other costs rose sharply. This is a well-managed company running into the structural ceilings of dairy: milk volume grows roughly with population, and pricing power against organised + cooperative competition is limited.
technical_read: Not pulled. Trades ~23-27x earnings; de-rated modestly as margins compressed.
sentiment_summary: Thread of 24 posts, all read; the primary tracker is ranvir (trusted, elevated), who has posted a detailed concall summary essentially every quarter for three years -- an unusually complete record. His tone shifted from 'very very bullish commentary' (Q4 FY24) to matter-of-fact reporting of margin compression through FY26. dark_hunter (trusted) wrote a strong 'hidden gem' bull note in Oct-2024 (essential product, pricing edge from farmer relationships, cash-rich, VAP + Africa optionality) -- but that predates the FY26 margin slide. Recent non-trusted posts (manomagg3) argue the market won't award a premium multiple until VAP is a much bigger share and the company can pass on procurement costs; questions raised about why Dodla is expanding in Africa when India is under-penetrated. No fresh trusted high-conviction call.

Strong FY25 (revenue +19%, PAT +56%); Africa and Orgafeed are higher-growth, higher-margin optionality
Disciplined procurement approach builds long-term farmer loyalty
Thorough, consistent trusted-user coverage every quarter
bear_case: FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to ~7.5% (two quarters at ~5%); couldn't pass on procurement costs
VAP mix slipped back to ~27% from ~35% -- the core margin-expansion thesis stalled
Structurally thin-margin, volume-capped business (milk volume ~ population growth)
~26-27x earnings is not cheap for a low-teens-ROE dairy with compressing margins
Rising employee/other costs; capital tied up in idle cash and a large greenfield capex
verdict_headline: A quality dairy operator hitting the structural margin and volume ceilings of the category -- FY26 margins compressed, VAP mix slipped; thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Low
verdict_reasoning: The recent-quarter trend is negative (margin compression, VAP mix down), so the small-cap 'recent inflection' carve-out does not apply -- and in any case this is a mid-cap in a structurally low-margin, volume-capped business. A 10x/100x outcome is not credible here. Thesis_fit 'neither'.
Not filtered on quality grounds -- balance sheet and management are genuinely good -- it simply does not fit the multi-bagger thesis.
